content.text: An AI-powered research assistant for Australian tax and compliance

SavvyWise aims to drastically reduce time spent on tax research, helping accountants reclaim their time and increase billable hours. I was approached by co-founder Agastya Patel to lead the design and user experience strategy during the product’s early development. Our roadmap includes expanding the platform's capabilities to encompass all aspects of accounting, including HR management.

content.heading: The Synergy
content.para: We operate on rapid design and development cycles. By gathering daily feedback from active users, we dissect core problems and brainstorm solutions in real-time. I then translate these insights into user flows and high-fidelity designs for developer handoff. This agile approach allows us to push improvements weekly, leveraging the flexibility of an early-stage startup to restructure major features whenever user feedback demands it.

content.heading: The Issues
content.para: Two months post-launch, we received critical feedback that the platform was providing inaccurate tax responses. Upon investigation, we discovered the root cause: the UI made it too easy for users to accidentally stay on the "General Tasks" model instead of switching to the dedicated "Tax Research" model. We realized that hiding model selection behind a simple dropdown was causing friction; users needed a clearer way to partition their work and verify which tool they were using.

content.caption: An interface revolving under a model dropdown

content.heading: The Solution
content.para: We realized that research and daily tasks are distinct mental modes for accountants, and the UI needed to reflect that. Following Agastya’s suggestion to separate these workflows, we moved away from a single interface. I applied a color-coding strategy to guide the user: the main Tax Research model shines in our brand yellow, secondary research tools are highlighted in orange, and general tasks remain in a clean black-and-white. This clear visual separation helps users instantly recognize which tool they are using.
